title: Regional capacity and data sovereignty intake checklist for enterprise failover requests
creator: Marcus Liu
description: Create a repeatable, operations-friendly intake checklist used by Sales, Solutions Engineering, and Customer Success to triage enterprise requests that combine new region availability with strict data residency or failover constraints. This ticket produces a checklist, scoring rubric, and routing rules for the intake form so requests are routed to the correct product stream (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) and include a preliminary capacity & cost band estimate. The output will be a single-page checklist doc, an intake form update spec, and example triage decisions for three realistic customer scenarios.
acceptance_criteria: Single-page intake checklist published in Confluence and linked in the PM playbook

Intake form fields defined and validated with Solutions Eng (fields: residency law citation, failover region pair, RTO/RPO, data-at-rest KMS requirement, expected qps and peak concurrency, retention window)
Automated routing rules documented: when to route to Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private and when to start enterprise sales engagement
Scoring rubric implemented in triage doc with explicit thresholds for capacity, latency, cost sensitivity and regulatory strictness
Three customer scenario walkthroughs reviewed and approved by Solutions Eng and Legal
Handoff checklist for Eng to onboard region is included (required logs, monitoring, SLA targets, runbook link)
steps: Interview 3 Solutions Engineers + 1 Sales AE to collect common asks and missing data points
Draft intake checklist and scoring rubric; share with Legal for data sovereignty phrasing
Prototype intake form JSON and update frontend field spec for Console & internal intake UI
Run 3 scenario tests (SaaS EU-only customer, Global enterprise with failover to US, Regulated APAC bank requiring on-prem) and iterate
Finalize checklist, publish Confluence doc, and add link to support template emails and intake ticketing flow
comments: 2026-03-10 Marcus Liu: Kickoff with Solutions Eng. Noted common missing field: expected peak concurrency. Agreed to add a mandatory throughput estimate field and a freeform legal citation field.
2026-03-11 Asha Patel (Solutions Eng): Feasibility note — Dedicated autoscale policy needs a pre-check for burst capacity; added as dependency to ENG-4321.

2026-03-11 Priya Nair (Legal): Reviewed draft language for 'data residency'; requested explicit mapping to jurisdiction and if egress restrictions apply. Legal suggests adding 'export control' checkbox.

2026-03-12 Leo Zhang (Engineering): Confirmed that runtime-1.20 has region onboarding hooks but cross-region KV replication is still experimental; recommend marking cross-region replication as 'requires eng evaluation' in checklist.
2026-03-12 Sofia Reynolds: Shared first draft at PM weekly; design asked for example UI for intake form; assigned DES-210 for mockups.
notes: Risk: Asking customers for accurate peak concurrency is often wrong; include guidance and a conservative estimation band to avoid over/under provisioning.
Tradeoff: More granular legal fields increase friction; aim for lightweight yes/no + citation field, escalate to Legal when score >= threshold.
Operationally important: Add a 'runbook readiness' tickbox to mark whether monitoring/dashboards exist before committing to SLA
Follow-up: Coordinate with Console team to expose 'region availability' mapping in customer-facing UI once routing rules are stable
